title: orchestration-overhead-latency-cost-roughs
content:
Purpose

Quick lab notes on how orchestration choices (routing, container lifecycle, and model variant stitching) add latency and $/1M-token cost beyond raw model inference. This is an internal working doc — short, informal, lots of open questions.

Motivation

We get repeated customer asks: why does the hosted API cost more than our per-GPU estimates? A lot of it is non-model overhead: routing decisions, health checks, container attach/detach, KV cache eviction work, and control-plane RPC chaining. Need a lightweight benchmark that isolates those layers and gives product a defensible set of numbers to cite in pricing/FAQ and to prioritize optimizations.

Experiment summary

Goals:
- Measure delta between pure-inference p50/p90/p99 and end-to-end request p50/p90/p99 when varying orchestration knobs.
- Back out incremental $/1M token attributable to orchestration overhead at our current cost model (gpu-hour + infra + infra-ops).

What we compare (3 axes):
A) Container lifecycle: warm-pool (W) vs ephemeral-spin (E) vs prewarmed-slab (S)
B) Routing policy: fastpath (single-hop policy) vs policy-fanout (multi-rule evaluation, fallback)
C) Model stitching: single-variant (no-stitch) vs dynamic-stitch (stitch to compact quantized variant on capacity pressure)

Testbed and method

- Model: open-7B-quant (representative medium LLM; ~30ms median pure decode on our test node for 64 token response)
- Hardware: single A40-like instance used for raw model baseline; the orchestration broker + router run on separate small nodes to emulate production split
- Load: 10k synthetic sessions, mix 80% short (<=32 tokens) / 20% medium (64-128 tokens), injected at steady 200 rps with microbursts to 800 rps for 10s every 60s
- Measurement: instrument client-observed wall clock per-request; trace tags for "orchestration_decision_ms", "container_attach_ms", "request_queue_ms", "model_decode_ms"; when unavailable we sample and reconstruct from logs.
- Cost model: use internal per-hour infra rates: GPU $4.40/hr (amortized), small control-plane node $0.28/hr; assume 1M tokens = approx 33k requests under our mix. Add networking egress negligible for these numbers.

Key raw baseline (pure inference)
(p50/p90/p99 for model-only decode on the test node)
- p50 model_decode_ms: 31ms
- p90 model_decode_ms: 78ms
- p99 model_decode_ms: 210ms

Aggregate E2E numbers (representative scenarios)
1) Warm-pool + fastpath + no-stitch (W / fastpath / no-stitch)  [closest to ideal] 
- p50 total_ms: 56ms
- p90 total_ms: 120ms
- p99 total_ms: 260ms
- median orchestration overhead: 25ms (routing + attach minimal)

2) Ephemeral-spin + fastpath + no-stitch (E / fastpath / no-stitch)  [higher attach cost] 
- p50 total_ms: 172ms
- p90 total_ms: 290ms
- p99 total_ms: 620ms
- median orchestration overhead: 140ms (container spin / cold start dominates)

3) Prewarmed-slab + policy-fanout + dynamic-stitch (S / fanout / stitch)  [complex routing & stitch] 
- p50 total_ms: 88ms
- p90 total_ms: 220ms
- p99 total_ms: 480ms
- median orchestration overhead: 57ms (policy eval + stitch switch + minor attach)

Simple ascii mini-plot (p90 latency in ms across scenarios)
(agents)   warm-pool   ephemeral   slab+fanout
p90       | 120ms     | 290ms     | 220ms
plot      W: ********** (120)
          E: ******************************* (290)
          S: ********************** (220)

Breakdown of overhead (approx median contributions, W/fastpath/no-stitch)
- routing decision: 8-12ms (policy table lookup, small RPCs)
- auth & quota checks: 2-6ms (local cache hits much cheaper)
- container attach / context switch: 6-8ms when warm; 120-260ms when ephemeral cold
- kv-cache lookup and prefix fetch: 3-10ms depending on hit/miss
- telemetry sampling/tracing overhead: 1-3ms (currently unbatched)

Cost attribution (back-of-envelope)
Assumptions:
- For our steady mix, 1M tokens ~ 33k requests (see load breakdown)
- Warm-pool policy keeps avg 4 warm containers per model in region; ephemeral-style uses vCPU-only control-plane for rapid spin-ups and keeps lower reserved GPU time but higher attach cost (wasted vCPU ops)

Compute pure GPU cost for decode (approx):
- Model-only GPU compute cost per 1M tokens = (GPU $4.40/hr * decoding_seconds_for_1M_tokens / 3600)
- From test: median decode 0.031s per short request; aggregated decode time for 1M tokens under mix -> ~1900s -> GPU cost = $4.40 * 1900/3600 = $2.32 (model compute only)

Add orchestration cost (infrastructure + wasted latency turning into scaling inefficiency):
- Warm-pool scenario: extra infra (control-plane + warm GPU idle amortized) ~ $1.10 per 1M tokens (keeping reserves/idle cycles)
- Ephemeral-spin scenario: infra ops + vCPU surge + repeated attach CPU work ~ $2.85 per 1M tokens (higher control-plane churn)
- Slab+fanout scenario: additional policy-eval expense, extra small nodes for dynamic-stitching ~ $1.90 per 1M tokens

Total $/1M (rounded):
- Warm-pool / fastpath / no-stitch: ~$3.42 / 1M tokens
- Ephemeral-spin / fastpath / no-stitch: ~$5.17 / 1M tokens
- Slab+fanout+stitch: ~$4.22 / 1M tokens

Interpretation / what product asks for
- Ephemeral/cold container strategy saves committed GPU hours but transfers cost to attach churn and user-perceived latency; for latency-sensitive tiers we should default to warm-pool.
- Complex policy fanouts + dynamic stitching give reasonable cost tradeoffs vs ephemeral: they add a midrange latency and midrange dollars but are useful for capacity-constrained environments.
- Routing decision path length correlates with p90 increases; even small RPC chains (2-3 small RPCs) add measurable ms under short responses.

Short checklist for optimization candidates (ranked)
1) Reduce cold attach cost: faster attach path, pre-attach token for hot sessions, reuse PID namespaces (big wins for ephemeral case)
2) Inline simple policy checks at edge (elide central fanout for common rules)
3) Batch telemetry writes or sample more aggressively to remove 1-3ms overhead per request
4) Make dynamic-stitch decision async where possible (respond with default variant and stitch in background, with progressive re-invocation)
5) Improve warm-pool packing heuristics to reduce idle GPU reserve cost while still keeping latency SLOs

Open questions / follow-ups
- Can we build a micro-binary that measures attach time in isolation across cloud providers? (ENG-XXXX)
- How much does TLS session reuse / keepalive affect small-request latency in our public API? Quick test: p95 delta expected ~3-8ms.
- Should pricing docs show a short table explaining orchestration delta per tier? Product wants a one-liner and a detailed appendix.

Notes to self
- Share with infra and product; ask infra to run an identical bench with our prod routing table (ticket: ENG-3340).
- Start a PR to add an attach-time histogram to observability surface (small change but high ROI).

Draft done — aiming to turn into a short one-pager for product with a single-page appendix of numbers.
summary: Working-bench notes quantifying orchestration layer latency/cost deltas. Shows that choice of warm-pool vs ephemeral and routing complexity materially affects p90/p99 and $/1M tokens. Action items included to reduce attach cost and inline common policy checks.
